newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Labour party dons law-and-order mantle.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Labour party dons law-and-order mantle.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour party, seeking to avert another Dunblane massacre, promised on Thursday to ban private ownership of handguns if it wins the coming general election.
In a speech to the party's annual conference, home affairs spokesman Jack Straw also declared war on drug-related crime.
Britain's streets could become as mean as America's unless Labour tackled crime and the inequalities that spawned it.
"We can't go on like this," said Straw, whose party has been taking a harder line on law and order to outflank the ruling Conservatives in the run-up to the election, due by next May.
"If you want a picture of what it could be like, of what happens if you don't get tough on crime and tough on the causes of crime, then look across the Atlantic.

"Look to see the wealthy barricade themselves in suburban fortresses, the poor trapped in ghettoes, millions owning guns for their self-defence and a prison population which has tripled in two decades," Straw said.

He said a Labour government would make sweeping changes to Britain's gun laws to avert a repeat of the Dunblane massacre in March, when a lone gunman mowed down 16 children and their teacher in a Scottish primary school before killing himself.

Labour, in opposition since 1979, would ban the private ownership and possession of all handguns, end mail order sales, ban all under-18s from holding airguns and shotguns, and introduce a stricter gun licensing system.
"We cannot have a society which values the right of civilians to own a handgun more than that of a child to a future," Straw said to loud applause.

Delegates later stood in a minute's silence to the victims of Dunblane after hearing an impassioned speech from Ann Pearston, who has been leading a campaign since the massacre for a total ban on handguns.
"We must shut the door on public safety tight -- so that it can't be pushed wider by the very powerful gun lobby in years to come," Pearston said.
On drugs, Straw pledged to make addicts undergo treatment and random drug tests in a bid to break the link with crime.

Straw said: "With heroin addicts thieving daily to fund their habit, at a cost of well over one billion pounds ($1.5 billion) in property stolen each year, it is time call a halt to this vicious circle of addiction and crime."
